_note: Normalisation rules for the school subjects named in occupations. Used by the website and the database seed.
generic: the two subjects you want to teach

about.Mathematics: The most widely required subject: engineering, technology, finance, science and many trades build on it.
about.Physics: Opens engineering, aviation, technology and the physical sciences.
about.Chemistry: Central to health, pharmacy, engineering, agriculture and laboratory careers.
about.Biology: The foundation for health, agriculture, veterinary and life-science careers.
about.English: Reading, writing and speaking well: every career relies on it, and many university programmes require it.
about.Literature in English: Builds reading, argument and writing for law, media and teaching.
about.Economics: Supports business, finance, policy and data careers.
about.Geography: Useful for environment, planning, logistics, tourism and public health.
about.History: Builds research and argument for law, policy, journalism and teaching.
about.Divinity: Supports social work, counselling, teaching and community roles.
about.Fine Art: Leads to design, architecture, media and creative industries.
about.Agriculture: Leads to farming, agronomy, extension work and agribusiness.
about.Entrepreneurship: Useful for business, marketing and starting your own enterprise.
about.Accounting: A direct start for accounting, auditing and finance.
about.Computer Studies: A head start for software, networks, IT support and data careers.
about.Technical Drawing: Supports architecture, engineering, carpentry and construction.
about.Woodwork: Hands-on preparation for carpentry and construction trades.
about.Metalwork: Hands-on preparation for welding, fabrication and mechanical trades.
about.Foods and Nutrition: Leads to cooking, catering and hospitality careers.
about.Foreign Language: Valuable in tourism, diplomacy and international business.
about.Statistics: Collecting, analysing and interpreting data: the base for data science, economics, research and public health.
about.Environmental Science: How natural systems work and how people affect them: leads to conservation, environmental health and planning.
about.Philosophy: Clear reasoning, argument and ethics: useful for law, policy, teaching and research.
about.Psychology: How people think, feel and behave: leads to counselling, health, education, management and marketing.
about.Sociology: How societies, groups and institutions work: leads to social work, policy, research and development work.
about.Government and Politics: How states, laws and public institutions work: leads to law, public administration and international affairs.
about.Business Studies: How organisations are run, marketed and financed: a base for management, marketing and starting a business.
about.Design and Technology: Designing and making products, from idea to prototype: leads to engineering, product and industrial design.
about.Music: Performance, composition and theory: leads to performance, production, teaching and sound engineering.
about.Drama and Theatre: Performance, storytelling and production: leads to acting, directing, media and teaching.
about.Media Studies: How media is made and how it shapes audiences: leads to journalism, film, communications and marketing.
about.Physical Education: Sport, fitness and the body: leads to coaching, sports science, physiotherapy and teaching.
